title: Yujin Securities lifts GS E&C target as 15t-won East Sea AI center advances - CHOSUNBIZ - Chosunbiz
content: Eugene Investment & Securities on the 13th said GS Engineering & Construction(36,000 won ▲ 800 2.27%) is seeing improved business visibility thanks to the Donghae AI data center (AIDC) push. It maintained its "Buy" recommendation and raised its target price 41% to 48,000 won from 34,000 won. Ryu Tae-hwan of Eugene Investment & Securities said, "GS Group is pushing to build a 1.2-gigawatt (GW) AI data center in the Bukpyeong No. 2 General Industrial Complex in Donghae, Gangwon Province," adding, "GS Holdings has established GS AI Infra for the data center business and incorporated it as a subsidiary, and plans to develop the project in phases to match tenant demand." The total project cost is expected to be about 15 trillion won based on 1.2 GW. Ryu said, "Advance procedures for groundbreaking are underway, including the start of the power system impact assessment and changes to the basic management plan, and if a prelease contract with the tenant under discussion is finalized, it will lead to project financing (PF) procurement and phase-one groundbreaking," analyzing that "visibility for groundbreaking is improving compared with when the project was announced." Ryu saw that, if a scenario of starting construction on a 150-megawatt (MW) data center every six months is applied, it could reduce GS Engineering & Construction's production capacity (CAPA) burden while securing a stable order backlog over a long period. Ryu estimated, "Assuming a 20-month construction period, construction cost of 1.5 trillion won per 150 MW, and an operating profit margin (OPM) of 8%, next year's revenue related to the Donghae AIDC would reach about 1.3 trillion won, with operating profit of about 100 billion won." Ryu also projected that the earnings gap from the sale of subsidiary GS Inima could be offset. Ryu said, "When the GS Inima sale is completed, 900 billion won in annual revenue and 120 billion won in operating profit will be excluded from consolidation results, but the Donghae AIDC will begin to replace the revenue gap from next year and offset a significant portion of the decline in operating profit," adding, "Considering the effects of balance sheet improvement and reduced financial expense, the profit gap on a pre-tax basis will narrow further." He added, "Although the final outcomes, such as the prelease contract and the GS Inima transaction completion, have not been confirmed and thus were not directly reflected in the earnings estimates, we present it as a second-tier preference stock within the construction sector by reflecting a narrower valuation discount driven by the data center momentum." title: GS The Fresh launches Mucho Más Starlight wines to tap Korea’s daily drinkers - CHOSUNBIZ - Chosunbiz
content: The supermarket GS The Fresh, operated by GS Retail(007070), said on the 13th that on the 12th it unveiled two "Mucho Más Starlight" wines, red and white, for the first time in Korea. Mucho Más is a wine brand whose name in Spanish means "more" and "much more." It is known as a daily wine that emphasizes value for money and is currently sold in 65 countries worldwide. Cumulative sales have surpassed 20 million bottles. The newly released "Mucho Más Starlight Red" adds vanilla and spice flavors to fruit aromas such as blackberry, raspberry, and cherry. It emphasizes soft tannins and a smooth texture. The white product adds tropical fruit flavors to aromas of peach, apricot, and citrus, and is characterized by fresh acidity and a vanilla finish. Each of the two products is priced at 22,900 won. To mark the launch, GS The Fresh will sell them at a discount of 19,900 won through the 18th. GS The Fresh's wine sales rose 9.8% in 2024 from a year earlier and then increased 19.6% last year. In the first half of this year, they also grew 27.4% from a year earlier, widening annual growth. Targeting this demand, GS The Fresh sells an average of about 40 types of wine per store, and some locations with an expanded assortment carry up to about 100 types. It plans to continue expanding its wine lineup around daily wines with strong value for money and exclusive items. Jun Jae-hyeok, GS Retail processed daily goods team MD, said, "Recently, wine has shed its image as a drink enjoyed only on special days and is becoming an everyday purchase made while grocery shopping," and added, "We will continue to strengthen our wine competitiveness by offering a wide variety, from value-for-money wines that can be enjoyed casually in daily life to differentiated products." title: CSM Switches to Aston Martin for Rest of GS Season - Sportscar365
content: CSM adds second entry for Houk, Ellahi for final three races; enters GT4 America for Indy… Czabok-Simpson Motorsport has made the switch from Porsche to Aston Martin GT4 machinery for the remainder of the IMSA Michelin Pilot Challenge season, while adding a second GS class entry in the process. The Indianapolis-based team, which has long been affiliated with running Porsches, will field two Aston Martin Vantage GT4 Evos beginning with next weekend’s round at Virginia International Raceway. While Gordon Scully and Morgan Burkhard will remain together in the No. 2 entry, Ayrton Houk as Ismaeel Ellahi will team up in the No. 3 Aston Martin for a three-race Pilot Challenge program. The shift to the British manufacturer is being billed as a “strategic move” according to a team statement, in order to get a jump start on the 2027 season. Sportscar365 understands CSM acquired one of Rebel Rock Racing’s Astons that it previously ran in the series. “Moving both cars to the Aston Martin now is an important step in our preparation for 2027,” said team co-owner Stephen Simpson. “It gives our engineers and drivers three race weekends to build a meaningful base of knowledge in Michelin Pilot Challenge conditions. “Ayrton has already tested with us several times and has consistently impressed the team with his pace, feedback and approach. “Ismaeel’s development in such a short period has been exceptional, and his CTMP victory showed that he is ready for this next challenge. “Gordon and Morgan give us the experience and continuity we need, so we believe these lineups create a very strong foundation for the rest of this season and for 2027.” Houk, 23, is additionally confirmed to also contest the Pirelli GT4 America season-ending rounds at Indianapolis Motor Speedway with CSM, with his co-driver yet to be announced. “The testing I have done with CSM gave me a real appreciation for how the team works and how committed everyone is to performance,” he said. “To now join the Michelin Pilot Challenge program for VIR, Indianapolis and Road Atlanta is a huge opportunity. “I am excited to share the No. 3 with Ismaeel, learn the Aston Martin quickly and contribute to the team’s preparation for 2027. “Adding the GT4 America finale at my home track in Indianapolis makes this four-race program even more special.” Ellahi, a 19-year-old American-Pakistani driver has been competing in VP Racing SportsCar Challenge competition, where he scored GSX class honors at Canadian Tire Motorsport Park in CSM’s first outing with the Aston Martin. “Two years ago, I was sim racing in my basement, and after only eight car races I am now preparing to make my Michelin Pilot Challenge debut,” he said. “Winning at CTMP was an unforgettable moment, but it also made me even more motivated for this next step. “I am grateful to CSM, my family, my partners and everyone who has helped me progress so quickly. “I am especially proud to represent my Pakistani heritage at this level, and I hope this opportunity shows other young drivers that there can be a path into professional motorsport even if they start in a simulator.” John Dagys is the founder and Editor-in-Chief of Sportscar365. title: Goldman Sachs buys NEOS in $2.25 billion deal to land $1 billion bitcoin yield ETF - CoinDesk
content:
Goldman Sachs is acquiring NEOS Investments, the firm behind BTCI, a $1.1 billion bitcoin synthetic exchange-traded fund (ETF) that yields roughly 27%, according to a senior ETF analyst at Bloomberg. The acquisition deal in cash and equity puts NEOS at a valuation of up to $2.25 billion, is subject to performance targets and is expected to close during the first quarter of 2027 pending regulatory approval, Goldman Sachs said Wednesday in a statement detailing the agreement. BTCI launched in October 2024 and has crossed $1 billion in assets in under two years, Eric Balchunas, a senior ETF analyst at Bloomberg, said in an X post. He also said it holds spot bitcoin exchange-traded products (ETPs) and sells call options against those positions to generate monthly distributions. It does not directly hold bitcoin, and investors receive the yield from the product but forfeit some of the upside when bitcoin rallies, he said.. That trade-off is exactly what Goldman filed to build itself four months ago, Balchunas added. On April 14, Goldman registered the Goldman Sachs Bitcoin Premium Income ETF with the SEC, proposing a structurally similar covered-call product. Balchunas was blunt about what Wednesday's deal means for that filing. "Nowww I get why GS never launched the BTC covered call product they filed months ago," Balchunas wrote. "Better to leapfrog BlackRock's $BITA vs me too?" One senior ETF analyst, who asked not to be named, said the deal reflects Goldman's push to build out its ETF business broadly, noting that BTCI is one of almost 20 funds in the NEOS lineup. "If anything, it shows that bitcoin is just part of the financial world, alongside stocks, bonds, etc." As of June 30, 2026, Goldman Sachs Asset Management, Innovator from Goldman Sachs Asset Management and NEOS manage more than $130 billion in ETF assets under supervision (AUS), according to the Wall Street bank’s statement. BlackRock released its own bitcoin income ETF, BITA, on Nasdaq on June 16, about two months ahead of Goldmine’s filing. BITA targets a 15-25% annual yield and sells covered calls on 25-35% of its IBIT holdings. Its expense ratio is 0.65%. BTCI charges 0.99% and is down 42.55% over the past year, with shares falling from a 52-week high of $65.87 to around $28.40, according to Bloomberg terminal data shared by Balchunas on X. According to the fund's SEC prospectus, BTCI's distributions may in part represent a return of capital rather than net investment income, a distinction income investors should weigh. Goldman's NEOS acquisition doesn't just hand it BTCI. It also grants it access to a $30 billion options-based ETF platform across 19 funds, one of the fastest-growing in the industry, the Wall Street giant’s statement said. Combined with Goldman's existing $40 billion in options-based ETF assets and the Innovator Capital Management acquisition it announced in December, Goldman will control more than $130 billion in total ETF assets, which is enough to rank it eighth among active ETF managers globally, it said. NEOS co-founders Troy Cates and Garrett Paolella will join Goldman as partners after closing. The derivative income ETF category has grown to roughly $180 billion in assets industry-wide, compounding at more than 70% annually since 2021, according to Morningstar. Goldman is buying into that growth rather than trying to organically replicate it. title: Oscar De La Rosa Defends Karol G’s ‘Alguien Que Te Amaba’ and Calls on Tejano Fans to ‘Stop Hating’ - Tejano Nation
content: La Mafia frontman says the cumbia’s ’90s-inspired sound is introducing Tejano music to new generations—and urges fans to celebrate artists who are taking the genre around the world Tejano music icon Oscar De La Rosa, the longtime frontman of internationally recognized Tejano supergroup La Mafia, is speaking out in support of Karol G’s “Alguien Que Te Amaba,” a cumbia co-written by the Colombian superstar, legendary Tejano singer-songwriter Pete Astudillo, and acclaimed songwriter-producer Edgar Barrera. The song has sparked conversation among Tejano fans, particularly over its unmistakable connection to the sound and spirit of Tejano cumbia from the 1990s. While some listeners have embraced Karol G’s interpretation as an opportunity to introduce elements of Tejano music to a massive global audience, others have questioned comparisons to the music of Selena and debated whether contemporary artists are appropriately representing the genre. For De La Rosa, however, the conversation should be less about comparisons and more about celebration. In a video shared on social media, the “Un Millón De Rosas” singer directly addressed those criticizing the song and urged fans to listen with an open mind. “¿Cómo es que no les gusta esa canción? ¿Qué pasa con ustedes? ¿Qué le pasa a los haters?” Translated to English, De La Rosa asked, “How can you not like that song? What’s wrong with you? What’s wrong with the haters?” He went on to defend Karol G, Astudillo and Barrera for creating a song that he believes is helping expose audiences outside the traditional Tejano community to a sound that shaped an important era of the genre. “Thank you for recording this song, because it is opening the eyes and ears of many people who have not heard our music,” De La Rosa said. He specifically pointed to the production’s ’90s influence, saying the song has “a lot of the style of our music from the ’90s.” That connection is particularly significant coming from De La Rosa, whose career with La Mafia spans decades of Tejano music’s evolution. Founded in Houston in 1980, La Mafia helped push Tejano beyond its traditional regional boundaries and became one of the genre’s most internationally successful groups. The band’s extensive touring in Mexico and Latin America helped establish a larger audience for Texas-based Tejano and Tex-Mex music. One of De La Rosa’s strongest messages was directed at the tendency to compare every successful female artist working within Tejano or Tejano-influenced music to Selena. “Why is it that whenever a woman records a song, they always want to compare her to Selena?” De La Rosa said. “Stop that. Come on. Give other people the opportunity to live their dream.” His comments echo a sentiment increasingly being voiced throughout the Latin music community: Selena’s legacy is monumental, but honoring her does not require placing every new female artist in her shadow. In the accompanying social media caption, De La Rosa reinforced that message, writing that “Selena will always have her place. Karol is writing her own story.” That distinction is important in the discussion surrounding “Alguien Que Te Amaba.” Rather than attempting to recreate Selena’s career or identity, Karol G is drawing inspiration from a musical tradition and introducing elements of that sound to listeners who may never have discovered the Tejano music of the 1990s. And having Astudillo—a songwriter whose work is deeply connected to Selena’s musical legacy—help bridge that generation gap makes the collaboration even more significant. “Alguien Que Te Amaba” arrives at a moment when Karol G is continuing to expand her musical palette. The song appears on her 2026 album No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto, released August 7, a project that represents a more introspective and experimental direction for the Colombian superstar. The collaboration with Astudillo gives the song a direct connection to the Tejano tradition, while Barrera brings his extensive experience as one of the most prominent songwriters and producers in contemporary Latin music. For many longtime Tejano fans, the song’s appeal is its familiarity. Its rhythmic character and musical flavor can evoke the golden era of Tejano cumbia while being presented through the voice and creative vision of one of today’s biggest Latin artists. De La Rosa believes that crossover can benefit the entire genre. He also pointed to Mexican-American group Frontera as another example of artists taking regional Mexican sounds to new audiences and said those efforts should be celebrated rather than criticized. “We have to be proud that someone out there loves what we’re doing, loves what we have done,” De La Rosa said, adding that he believes Selena herself would have been proud to see the music reaching new audiences. De La Rosa’s comments also touch on a larger issue facing Tejano music: gatekeeping. For decades, Tejano has maintained a fiercely loyal fan base that has protected its history, sound and cultural identity. That passion has helped preserve the music through changing musical trends and generations. But there is a difference between preserving a genre and preventing it from evolving. When fans insist that Tejano must sound exactly as it did during its commercial peak, emerging artists can find themselves caught between honoring the music’s roots and creating something that reflects their own generation. That tension is especially important today as younger Tejano artists incorporate elements of regional Mexican, pop, urban, electronic and other contemporary sounds into their music. Rather than viewing those influences as a threat to Tejano, De La Rosa’s message suggests they can be viewed as another chapter in the genre’s ongoing story. “That’s the reason why Tejano music came to an end, because of you haters that don’t allow it to continue to grow and become world-known music again.” Whether one agrees completely with De La Rosa’s assessment of Tejano’s decline, his larger point is difficult to ignore: a genre cannot reach new audiences if its own community rejects every attempt to take it somewhere new. De La Rosa is uniquely positioned to make that argument. Born in Houston, Oscar De La Rosa is best known as the lead vocalist of La Mafia, the Grammy-winning group he helped establish in 1980 alongside his brother Leonardo Gonzales and keyboardist and accordionist Armando Lichtenberger Jr. La Mafia emerged from Houston’s Northside and developed a distinctive sound that blended Tejano, cumbia, pop and other Latin influences. The group eventually expanded its reach throughout Mexico, Latin America and beyond, helping demonstrate that a Texas-based Tejano act could build an international audience. The band’s achievements include Grammy and Latin Grammy recognition, along with numerous Tejano Music Awards and Premio Lo Nuestro honors. La Mafia remains active, with De La Rosa continuing as its lead vocalist. In other words, De La Rosa isn’t speaking about musical evolution from the sidelines. He spent his career helping evolve Tejano music himself. De La Rosa concluded his message with a plea for fans to change the way they approach new artists and new interpretations of Tejano music. “Give someone else a chance,” he said. “Stop what you’re doing. Stop hating.” That message may be the most important takeaway from the debate surrounding “Alguien Que Te Amaba.” Tejano music has a rich history worth protecting. Selena’s legacy deserves to be celebrated. Pete Astudillo’s contributions deserve recognition. The music of La Mafia and the artists who built the genre deserve their place in history. But the next generation deserves room to create, too. If Karol G’s “Alguien Que Te Amaba” introduces millions of listeners to the sound of Tejano cumbia, perhaps the question should not be whether it sounds exactly like the music of the past. Perhaps the better question is where those new listeners go next. If they discover Selena, Astudillo, La Mafia, David Lee Garza, Mazz, La Sombra, Emilio Navaira and the countless artists who helped build Tejano—and then discover today’s emerging Tejano artists—the genre gains something far more valuable than nostalgia. It gains new listeners, new artists and another generation. As De La Rosa put it in his social media message: “Music is not compared, it is celebrated.” And for a genre that has spent years fighting to remain visible, that may be exactly the attitude Tejano music needs to move forward. title: Prosecution concludes arguments against banned AL GS Quader, 7 others - Just News BD
content: The prosecution has concluded its arguments against banned Awami League General Secretary Obaidul Quader and seven other senior leaders of the Awami League, Jubo League and Chhatra League in the case over crimes against humanity occurred during July Revolution at the International Crimes Tribunal. A three-member judicial panel of International Crimes Tribunal-2, headed by Chairman Justice Nazrul Islam Chowdhury, concluded the arguments on Wednesday. Chief Prosecutor Md Aminul Islam and Prosecutor Gazi MH Tamim presented the arguments for the prosecution. Lawyers Lokman Howlader and Ishrat Jahan are representing the accused as state-appointed defence counsel. Journalist Ashraf Kaiser testified before the tribunal on July 26. In his testimony, he described the Awami League's long rule and the July Revolution. The first round of testimony in the case concluded on April 27, after which a date was set for arguments. However, the prosecution later sought to record Ashraf Kaiser's testimony, and the tribunal allowed the application. The investigation officer subsequently testified again. Besides Obaidul Quader, the other accused are Awami League Joint General Secretary AFM Bahauddin Nasim; former state minister for information and broadcasting Mohammad Ali Arafat; Jubo League President Sheikh Fazle Shams Parash and General Secretary Mainul Hossain Khan Nikhil; and Chhatra League President Saddam Hossain and General Secretary Wali Asif Inan. All the accused are absconding. On January 22, Tribunal-2 ordered the start of the trial after framing charges against the seven accused. On December 18, 2025, the tribunal took cognizance of the formal charges filed by the prosecution. The prosecution began presenting its arguments in the case on August 4. According to the prosecution, the accused issued coordinated instructions, incited violence and delivered provocative speeches to suppress the July-August movement. They allegedly planned violence through several meetings and called on leaders and activists to take to the streets to resist the movement. The prosecution further alleged that the accused played roles in armed attacks, severe repression and media control in several areas, resulting in killings, attempted killings and widespread violence across the country. The prosecution argued that these acts constitute crimes against humanity.

Goldman Sachs Group Inc (NYSE:GS, XETRA:GOS) will acquire exchange-traded funds provider Neos Investments in a deal valued at up to $2.25 billion, the bank said Wednesday, deepening its push into the fast-growing derivative income ETF market. The Connecticut-based ETF issuer manages roughly $30 billion across 19 options-based income ETFs, according to data cited by Jefferies. The acquisition follows Goldman's deal late last year to buy ETF operator Innovator Capital Management for $2 billion. Once the Neos transaction closes, Goldman's combined ETF assets will total $130 billion. The deal, expected to close in the first quarter of 2027, will be paid in a mix of cash and equity, with a portion tied to asset retention and performance targets, according to Jefferies. Neos co-founders Troy Cates and Garrett Paolella will join Goldman Sachs Asset Management as partners when the deal closes, with the rest of the Neos team expected to follow. Neos specializes in systematic options-based income strategies, writing index option overlays on equity, fixed income and alternative exposures within a tax-efficient ETF structure. Its flagship funds include SPYI, the S&P 500 High Income ETF with about $11.3 billion in assets; QQQI, the Nasdaq-100 High Income ETF with about $13.9 billion; and IWMI, the Russell 2000 High Income ETF with about $1.1 billion. The firm has also launched hedged equity, alternatives and enhanced fixed income products, including its bitcoin-linked BTCI fund. Neos has posted year-to-date inflows of about $13 billion. Jefferies noted that the four largest funds have seen annualized organic growth well above industry levels, with QQQI up 143%, IWMI up 236%, BTCI up 104% and SPYI up 101% as of July 31. As a percentage of assets under management, Goldman is paying about 7.5% for Neos, in line with its Innovator Capital acquisition at roughly 7.1% of AUM and above older deals for specialty ETF franchises struck before the rise of active and derivatives-based ETFs. The derivative income ETF category has grown to about $180 billion in industry-wide assets, compounding at more than 70% annually since 2021, according to Morningstar data cited by Jefferies. Combined with its existing options-based ETF lineup, the acquisition positions Goldman Sachs Asset Management among the top eight active ETF providers, with about $80 billion in active ETF assets. title: CDS' WeeAI Platform Receives Top-Tier GS Certification - thelec.net
content: South Korean AI company CDS said its integrated AI platform, WeeAI v1.6.0, has received Grade 1 certification under the GS (Good Software) certification program from the Korea Testing & Research Institute (KTR). WeeAI allows users to access and compare more than 30 AI models from nine major providers within a single environment. Supported models include those from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, SpaceX (xAI), Perplexity, Mistral, Meta and Alibaba. According to CDS, one of the platform's key features is multi-model simultaneous response, which enables a single prompt to be submitted to as many as three AI models at the same time. Users can compare differences in reasoning, perspective, expression and information quality before selecting the response best suited to their needs. The company said the feature helps reduce dependence on any single AI model and allows organizations to choose different models depending on tasks such as planning, research, analysis, translation, education and content creation. CDS describes WeeAI as an AI orchestration and operations platform designed to centrally manage AI accounts, costs, permissions and security policies across an organization. A key component of the platform is its shared credit-based billing system. Rather than requiring individual users to maintain separate subscriptions for multiple AI services, WeeAI enables organizations to purchase a common pool of credits that are deducted based on actual usage. Administrators can allocate credits by organization, department, group or user, while also controlling access to specific AI models and functions, setting usage limits and monitoring consumption. The platform additionally supports the distribution of shared prompts and organization-specific templates. CDS said the usage-based model can reduce costs associated with uneven utilization, inactive accounts and duplicate subscriptions while providing data-driven budgeting. If paid credits are exhausted, users can continue working through supported free AI models. According to the company, WeeAI offers nine generative AI work environments, including AI chat, presentations, documents, spreadsheets, images, videos, music, code generation and drawing tools. The platform supports output formats commonly used by Korean public-sector and educational institutions, including HWPX, DOCX, PDF, PPTX and XLSX. The platform can be deployed in cloud, dedicated private cloud, on-premises or hybrid environments depending on an organization's security policies and IT infrastructure. CDS said WeeAI also includes personally identifiable information (PII) detection and protection functions, knowledge base and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) integration for incorporating internal organizational data into AI responses, and support for single sign-on (SSO) and organizational directory integration. Looking ahead, the company plans to add capabilities such as automatic AI model recommendation and routing based on task characteristics, credit usage forecasting and budget controls, institutional prompt asset management, integration with legal and public data sources, account lifecycle management and industry-specific AI agents. GS certification is South Korea's national software quality certification program. Under the Software Promotion Act, software is evaluated across multiple criteria, including functional suitability, performance efficiency, compatibility, usability, reliability, security, maintainability and portability.

title: Citroen Built A Rotary GS, Then Tried To Buy Them All Back And Crush Them - Carscoops
content:
One of just 847 GS Birotors is heading to auction, alongside the even rarer rotary prototype that started the whole adventure The 1970s rotary gold rush persuaded everyone from GM to Mercedes that pistons were old news. Citroen jumped aboard too, only to eventually decide its rotary GS was something it would rather forget. It even tried buying the cars back so it could destroy them. Related: Citroen’s Iconic 2CV Is Coming Back As A $17,000 EV Fortunately, some owners didn’t cooperate. One of the survivors is this 1973 GS Birotor being offered without reserve by Broad Arrow at The Quail Auction, where its $20,000 to $30,000 estimate makes it look suspiciously affordable among Monterey Car Week‘s seven-figure exotica. The regular GS was already wilfully unconventional, with slippery styling and Citroen’s famous hydropneumatic suspension. It was deservedly named European Car of the Year in 1971. But through Comotor, its rotary joint venture with Germany’s NSU, Citroen stuffed in a twin-rotor Wankel derived from the technology used in the NSU Ro 80. The 2.0-liter unit produced 105 hp (106 PS) and drove through a three-speed semi-automatic transmission. Unfortunately, the Birotor arrived just as the 1973 oil crisis made thirsty cars about as fashionable as narrow-leg pants. It was also enormously expensive, costing almost as much as Citroen’s grander DS. Just 847 were built before more conservative Peugeot took control of troubled Citroen and decided the rotary experiment wasn’t worth supporting. But the new bosses went further than merely axing the Birotor. Rather than keep supplying parts for a tiny population of troublesome cars, Citroen attempted to buy Birotors back and scrap them. Broad Arrow says roughly 250 are thought to survive today. This example formerly belonged to the Mullin Automotive Museum and shows an incredible 1,080 miles (1,740 km). But for Citroen geeks, this Monterey find gets even more tempting. Because Broad Arrow is also auctioning a 1970 M35 (see bottom two galleries), the road-going laboratory that preceded the Birotor. Its unusual Heuliez-built 2+2 body hides hydropneumatic suspension and a tiny 995 cc single-rotor Wankel. Citroen built only 267 M35s, loaning examples to selected customers who effectively became development drivers. It later bought back and destroyed many of those too. This Mullin Museum alumnus has covered 11,600 miles (18,704 km) and is estimated to fetch $30,000 to $40,000. So while collectors nearby fight over another million-dollar Porsche, you could conceivably spend around $50,000 and take home two incredibly rare survivors from one of Citroen’s wildest engineering dead ends. Winning mandates on large transactions not only supports advisory revenues but can also generate opportunities across financing, underwriting and other client businesses. Recent league-table rankings highlight that strength. Goldman was the only adviser in South and Central America to exceed $10 billion in aggregate deal value during the first half of 2026, according to GlobalData. It also ranked first among North American M&A advisers by deal value, advising on $437.7 billion of transactions. The favorable M&A backdrop led Goldman to deliver strong results. GS’s IB fees rose 52% year over year in the first half of 2026, driven by higher advisory, equity underwriting and debt underwriting revenues amid improving capital markets activity. Management also sounded constructive about the operating environment following the second-quarter results. CEO David Solomon highlighted accelerating momentum across the company’s businesses and pointed to strong client demand for Goldman to advise on major strategic transactions. Management noted that the investment banking backlog reached its highest level in five years, including a record advisory backlog, supported by robust strategic M&A activity, AI-related capital formation and stronger financing demand. AI-Led Initiative to Transform Business: GS is undertaking an ambitious, firmwide artificial intelligence (AI) transformation aimed at boosting fee income, improving productivity and expanding long-term operating leverage. The initiative spans its core businesses, including trading, investment banking, asset management and internal operations, positioning AI as a central growth driver. Last month, Yahoo Finance, citing Reuters, reported that Goldman Sachs Asset Management had launched AlphaAI, an artificial intelligence-focused investment platform. The initiative underscores the firm's conviction that AI will emerge as a significant driver of investment opportunities and returns across both public and private markets. Earlier, Goldman partnered with Anthropic on a $1.5-billion initiative designed to accelerate AI adoption across hundreds of portfolio companies. At the center of Goldman’s transformation are two major initiatives — One Goldman Sachs 3.0, or OneGS 3.0, and the GS AI Assistant program. OneGS 3.0 is a multi-year effort to integrate AI into the firm’s core operating model rather than treat it as a standalone technology. The program focuses on simplifying workflows, modernizing infrastructure and supporting scalable growth through shared platforms, standardized processes and higher-quality data. The GS AI Assistant is expected to further improve employee productivity by helping professionals analyze information, generate content and complete routine tasks more efficiently. As adoption expands, the platform could reduce manual workloads and allow employees to devote more time to client engagement, decision-making and higher-value activities. Management has expressed strong confidence in AI’s long-term potential. Although spending on AI, data and digital infrastructure may keep expenses elevated in the near term, the investments could generate meaningful productivity gains and help the firm move toward its medium-term efficiency ratio target of 60%. Strategic Streamlining Pays Off: The company’s streamlining efforts have been underway for some time as it retreats from the underperforming consumer banking ventures. Under CEO David Solomon, GS has embarked on a deliberate transformation to exit non-core consumer banking and double down on the divisions wherein Goldman maintains a clear competitive advantage. In sync with its restructuring efforts, in April 2026, the company acquired Innovator Capital Management, expanding its active ETF capabilities as part of a broader strategy to build durable revenue streams through diversified asset and wealth management offerings.  In the same month, Goldman completed the divestiture of its Polish asset management business, Goldman Sachs TFI, to ING Bank Slaski, further streamlining its asset management operations. In the third quarter of 2025, the company transitioned the General Motors credit card program. These moves demonstrate a well-thought-out exit, allowing the company to reallocate capital and attention toward higher-margin, more scalable businesses like Global Banking and Markets, and the asset and wealth management divisions. Robust Liquidity Aids Capital Distribution: GS maintains a fortress balance sheet, with the Tier 1 capital ratios well above regulatory requirements. This financial strength allows it to return capital to its shareholders aggressively through buybacks and a healthy dividend yield. As of June 30, 2026, cash and cash equivalents were $187 billion, while deposits totaled $558 billion. Total unsecured debt (comprising long-term and short-term borrowings) was $438 billion, of which only $90 billion was near-term borrowings. Following the Federal Reserve’s 2026 stress test, the company increased its quarterly common stock dividend by 11% to $5 per share beginning in the third quarter of 2026. The company also has a share repurchase plan in place. In the first quarter of 2025, the board approved a share repurchase program of up to $40 billion of common stock. As of June 30, 2026, Goldman had $21.6 billion worth of shares available under authorization. Including dividends, GS’s total return over the past three years has been 206.3% compared with the industry’s average of 132.3%, and JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley’s averages of 132.5% and 146.6%, respectively. Thus, the combination of potential capital appreciation, dependable dividend income and continued share repurchases enhances the stock’s total-return prospects. Supported by Goldman’s robust liquidity and capital levels, its shareholder payout activities appear sustainable. Analysts are bullish on GS. Over the past 30 days, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for 2026 and 2027 earnings has been revised upward. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Goldman’s 2026 and 2027 earnings implies year-over-year growth of 34.2% and 4.9%, respectively. The GS stock currently trades at a premium to the industry. The stock is trading at a forward price/earnings (P/E) of 14.58X above the industry average of 14.08X. Its peers JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley are trading at a P/E of 14.41X and 16.63X, respectively. Goldman is well-positioned to benefit from stronger capital markets volumes and a record IB backlog. Its leading M&A franchise, rising IB fees and upward earnings estimate revisions further support the growth outlook. The company’s focus on AI, productivity and strategic streamlining should also strengthen long-term profitability. By exiting less attractive businesses and prioritizing higher-return Global Banking & Markets and Asset & Wealth Management operations, Goldman could improve earnings quality. Its strong capital and liquidity position also supports continued dividends and share repurchases. Though GS valuation looks expensive, this premium appears justified by the company’s leading M&A position, improving earnings outlook and strong execution. Overall, the GS stock appears to be a compelling buy for investors with a medium- to long-term horizon. Although the stock’s strong recent performance may lead to periodic volatility, any meaningful pullback could offer an attractive entry point for investors seeking exposure to a premier global investment-banking franchise. title: 10 BMW Motorcycles Worth Every Penny - Top Speed
content: In the American motorcycle market, BMW Motorrad offers one of the most diverse lineups of bikes. These range from luxury tourers to do-it-all adventure bikes to retro-vibing roadsters and track-going monsters. At the same time, BMW surprisingly keeps the value quotient in check (particularly from a European bikemaker context), and most of its bikes are worth each penny you pay. We're talking about 10 such bikes, ranging from touring bikes with Japanese reliability to adventure bikes that excel at everything. There's something for everyone here. This list is organized in descending order of pricing. BMW offers the best of two-wheeled luxury, comfort, and performance with the K 1600 GTL. This full dresser brings the best of "big" American luxury charm with sophisticated technology to offer a surprisingly versatile land yacht. A unique six-cylinder engine powers the K 1600 GTL. This 1,649 cc mill produces 160 horsepower at 6,750 RPM and 132.7 pound-feet at 5,250 RPM. Power is sent to the rear wheel via a six-speed manual coupled to a final shaft drive system. For the chassis, a cast-aluminum bridge-type frame is present. It is suspended on BMW's famed Duolever front suspension with a central spring strut and 4.5 inches of travel. The rear gets the Paralever setup, coupled to a cast-iron single-sided swingarm and 5.3 inches of travel. Technology features are galore, too. Notable ones include a huge 10.25-inch TFT, a four-button cluster for custom functions, dynamic traction control, three ride modes, dynamic electronic suspension, hill start control, heated grips and seats, and an audio system, among others. This is arguably the most value-packed luxury touring motorcycle, and it undercuts the Honda Gold Wing, despite being more powerful. The 1,649 cc mill mentioned above is present here as well, in the same exact tune. Power is sent to the rear wheel via a six-speed manual and a final shaft drive neatly hidden in its single-sided swingarm. The chassis is also similar to the GTL, featuring the bridge-type cast aluminum frame. As for suspension, the front gets a double-wishbone (Duolever) with 4.5 inches of travel. The rear gets a monoshock (Paralever) setup with 5.3 inches of travel. The suspension offers electronic adjustability and even an automatic load-leveling feature. There is no dearth of top-spec technology. The K 1600 B gets a huge 10.25-inch TFT with a wide range of connectivity and integrated map navigation features. Other notable features include three ride modes, dynamic traction control, hill start control, and engine brake control, among others. This futuristic-looking touring bike makes luxury feel practical. The same boxer twin powers the R 1300 RT as on the go-anywhere R 1300 GS. The 1,300 cc mill produces 145 horsepower at 7,750 RPM and 110 pound-feet of torque at 6,500 RPM, sent to the wheel via a six-speed manual gearbox coupled to a final Cardan shaft drive system for added durability. Underpinning the R 1300 RT is a two-part frame with the engine utilized as a stressed member. It is suspended on BMW's famed Telelever front and Paralever rear suspension setups with 5.8 inches of front and 6.2 inches of rear travel. Adding to its versatility is a factory-adjustable seat, solid wind protection, and commendable technology. Notable features include keyless ride, dynamic electronic stability control, heated grips, and a gorgeous-looking 10.25-inch TFT with Bluetooth navigation as standard. This BMW adventure bike is famed for being a flagship that can do it all exceptionally well. Powering the flagship GS is the 1,300 cc liquid-cooled mill, which produces 145 horsepower at 7,750 RPM and 110 pound-feet at 6,500 RPM. Power is sent to the rear wheel via a standard six-speed manual with a final Cardan shaft drive system. It can also be equipped with an optional automatic transmission. Underpinning the R 1300 GS is a sophisticated setup. It comprises a pressed-steel main frame utilizing the engine as a stressed member. It is suspended on a double-wishbone suspension setup up front with 7.5 inches of travel. The rear gets a link-type monoshock with 7.8 inches of travel. BMW has loaded the R 1300 GS to the brim with technology features. Notable ones include four ride modes, dynamic traction control, dynamic brake control, dynamic cruise control, and hill start control. The dashboard comprises a sizable 6.5-inch TFT. The BMW S 1000 RR is a surprisingly affordable sports bike that is cheaper than a Honda Fireblade. Powering the S 1000 RR is a proven inline-four engine that produces 205 horsepower at 13,000 RPM and 83 pound-feet of torque at 11,000 RPM. It is coupled to a WSBK-derived quick throttle as standard as part of its latest update. Underpinning the flagship BMW sportbike is a lightweight twin-spar aluminum frame, coupled to a race-derived aluminum swingarm and subframe. The frame is suspended on 45 mm inverted front forks with 4.7 inches of travel, alongside a monoshock with 4.6 inches of travel. Both ends offer full adjustability. Cutting-edge technology such as six ride modes, pit lane limiter, launch control, dynamic traction control, wheelie control, and slide control is present, too. This BMW crossover feels worth every dollar because it blends urban mobility, highway runs, and even spirited mountain sessions so seamlessly. The S 1000 XR packs a proper superbike engine derived from the S 1000 RR. The 999 cc liquid-cooled inline-four mill produces 170 horsepower at 11,000 RPM and 84 pound-feet of torque at 9,250 RPM. Power is sent to the rear wheel via a six-speed manual gearbox. Underpinnings comprise a bridge-type cast aluminum frame, using the engine as a load-bearer, suspended on long-travel springs. The front gets 45 mm inverted forks with 5.9 inches of travel, and the rear comprises a monoshock with 5.9 inches of travel. Its electronic, self-adjusting rebound settings at both ends instill sharp cornering confidence. Technology features are plentiful and stitch its do-it-all character together. This is BMW's arch-nemesis to the Triumph Scrambler 1200. The R 12 G/S is powered by a mighty 1,170 cc boxer twin engine with 109 horsepower at 7,000 RPM and 85 pound-feet of torque at 6,500 RPM. Power is sent to the rear wheel via a six-speed manual gearbox coupled to a final Cardan shaft drive system for added durability. The engine sits in a tubular space frame and is suspended on long-travel suspension. The front gets 45 mm inverted forks with 8.2 inches of travel, and the rear gets a monoshock with 7.8 inches of travel. Both ends are fully adjustable. This is further complemented by durable aluminum cross-spoke wheels wrapped with all-terrain tires. The R 12 G/S gets a slew of assistive technology features. Notable ones include riding modes, dynamic traction control, cornering ABS, dynamic engine brake control, and partial integral brake system. This classic cruiser bike matches the essence of American big twins but with a unique twist: a large air-oil-cooled boxer-twin engine instead of a V-twin. In fact, it is the largest production motorcycle flat twin until the much-anticipated production-spec R 20 breaks cover. The 1,802 cc mill produces 91 horsepower at 4,750 RPM and 120 pound-feet of torque at 3,000 RPM. Adding to its heavy-duty outlook is a double-loop steel main frame with bolted beams. A twin-sided steel swing arm is part of the chassis and adds to its stretched-out stance. The R 18 gets telescopic forks up front with 4.7 inches of travel. The rear comprises a hidden monoshock that seems to be strongly inspired by the Harley Softail series. Owing to its old-school charm, BMW has added very little technology to the R 18, with notable features being LED lighting and a USB Type-C port only. This is a gravely overlooked BMW naked bike that offers grin-worthy performance at a bargain price. It is powered by the same 999 cc inline-four liquid-cooled engine as the S 1000 RR, but subtracts the ShiftCam for a more peaky output of 170 horsepower at 11,000 RPM and 84 pound-feet of torque at 9,250 RPM. Power is sent to the rear wheel via a six-speed manual gearbox coupled to a standard slipper clutch. The chassis components are also S 1000 RR derived, featuring inverted 45 mm forks up front with full adjustability and 4.7 inches of travel and a fully adjustable monoshock with 4.6 inches of travel. With a curb weight of as low as 432.1 pounds, the power-to-weight ratio is commendable on this Beamer. The S 1000 R is further tamed with a slew of top-spec electronics, such as M Quick action throttle, engine drag torque control, and three riding modes. BMW also packs a TFT display with smartphone connectivity as standard fitment. This BMW adventure bike balances ruggedness, comfort, and versatility. The F 900 GS takes flight in the heated middleweight segment and shines bright. A versatile 270-degree parallel-twin engine powers it. This liquid-cooled 895 cc mill produces 105 horsepower at 8,500 RPM and 68.6 pound-feet of torque at 6,750 RPM. As for the chassis, ​​​​​​​you get a bridge-type main frame coupled to a steel bolt-on subframe and a cast aluminum twin-sided swingarm.​​​​​​​ This is coupled to 43 mm inverted front forks with full adjustability and 9.05 inches of travel. The rear gets a monoshock with preload and rebound adjustability and 8.46 inches of travel. To match its go-anywhere attitude, it gets a 21/17-inch spoked wheel combination wrapped around all-purpose tires. The technology suite is stacked with notable features like dynamic traction control, a standard Akrapovic sport muffler, rain and road riding modes, heated grips, and a 6.5-inch TFT with Bluetooth connectivity. title: GS Holdings’ Q2 operating profit surges 253% on strong refining margins - koreajoongangdaily.com
content: GS Holdings posted a 253.4 percent surge in second quarter operating profit as stronger refining margins, higher oil prices and robust lubricant earnings lifted results above market expectations. GS Holdings reported a 253.4 percent surge in quarterly operating profit for the April-to-June period on year upon higher international oil prices and rising export prices for petroleum products. The company on Tuesday reported an operating profit of 1.71 trillion won ($1.21 billion) for the second quarter of 2026, beating the market consensus of 1.12 trillion won, compiled by market tracker FnGuide. The holding company, which owns oil refiner GS Caltex, also reported increases in both revenue and net profit. Quarterly revenue rose 24.9 percent year on year to 7.41 trillion won, while net profit surged 1,180.5 percent to 1.13 trillion won. Compared to the first quarter of 2026, revenue rose 8.3 percent from 6.84 trillion won, operating profit increased 36.5 percent from 1.26 trillion won and net profit climbed 36.9 percent from 826.7 billion won. For the first half of the year, GS's operating profit was reported at 2.98 trillion won, up 130.8 percent from the year prior. Revenue rose 17.2 percent and net profit jumped 415.6 percent during the same period. GS attributed the sharp improvement in its consolidated second quarter results largely to strong earnings at GS Caltex. “This was driven by wider refining margins amid higher international oil prices and export prices for petroleum products, as well as a temporary inventory effect,” GS said. “In particular, the lubricants business posted record-high earnings due to global supply disruptions.” It added that operating profit from GS Energy’s resource development business also increased on the back of higher oil prices. The petrochemical business, however, swung to an operating loss from the previous quarter as higher naphtha costs were not fully reflected in product prices, according to GS. Its power generation subsidiaries — GS EPS and GS E&R — also posted weaker results due to lower system marginal prices and operating rates. “Oil prices are expected to remain volatile in the third quarter due to developments in the Middle East, while the temporary inventory effect is also expected to fade,” the company said. “How flexibly we respond to these uncertainties will affect our performance.” A National Assembly report finds young Koreans with low or unstable incomes are most likely to lose government benefits after quitting savings plans early. Korea's youth employment rate fell in July, while youth unemployment climbed to 6.8 percent. This marked the second consecutive month of gains. Additionally, the number of employed people stood at 29.13 million in July, compared to 29.02 million a year earlier. Ryoo Sang-dai, whose three-year term ends Aug. 20, said earlier lessons impel the central bank to take a pre-emptive monetary policy response.

title: Cicero, MMR Split Up From Pilot Challenge GS Points Lead - dailysportscar.com
content: ShareFacebook, Twitter, Google Plus, Pinterest, Email IMSA Michelin Pilot Challenge GS Championship leader Nate Cicero has parted ways with McCumbee McAleer Racing (MMR) and announced an indefinite hiatus from motorsport with only three races left in the 2026 season. Cicero, a member of the 2026 Ford Racing Driver Development Team, joined MMR’s Pilot Challenge programme midway through the 2025 season and helped the team capture its first Michelin Pilot Challenge victory last year at Road America. After helping co-driver Jenson Altzman secure fourth in the 2025 GS (Grand Sport) standings, Cicero joined undefeated Mustang Challenge North America champion Robert Noaker for the 2026 campaign. Through seven races, the drivers of the #13 Ford Mustang GT4 combined for three podium finishes, and a best finish of second at Watkins Glen. After last week’s race at Road America, those results gave Cicero and Noaker a 100-point lead in the GS (Grand Sport) standings. On 6 August, Cicero abruptly announced his departure from the sport, saying: “I will be taking a leave from racing to focus on personal matters and would appreciate privacy at this time. I want to thank everyone who supported me over the years.” Five days later on 10 August, MMR released its own statement regarding Cicero’s departure. “We are disappointed to announce that our relationship with Nate Cicero has come to an end. Effective immediately, Nate is no longer associated with MMR in any capacity. We will have no further comment on the topic,” the team said. “We remain focused on moving forward and continuing to build on MMR’s goals and success. As we look to our future, we will be making a driver announcement in the coming days.” Ford Racing was also approached by DSC and declined to comment. As a child in karting ten years ago, Cicero was mentored by MMR co-owner Stevan McAleer and his brother Stuart. Cicero’s affiliation with MMR continued into his graduation to the Whelen Mazda MX-5 Cup, where he took Rookie of the Year honours in 2023, finished sixth in the standings, then improved to fourth in 2024. That is the mantra for Head Coach Nick Hart's Gibson Southern High School Football Titans entering the 2026 season. In 2025, the Titans posted a 12-2 (6-0 Pocket Athletic Large-School Division) season that featured PAC Large-School Division, two victories over No. 1-ranked teams IHSAA Class 3A Sectional 32 and IHSAA South Regional championships before falling just shy on the road against eventual IHSAA Class 3A State Champion Cascade in the 3A South Semi-State. Following graduation of a highly successful group of seniors, Hart looks for the Titans’ Class of 2027 seniors to lead a relatively inexperienced to varsity football team that, following the program’s Maroon-and-Gold game at Jack Jewell Memorial Field Aug. 8, hosts Evansville Central Aug. 14 in an IHSAA preseason scrimmage ahead of the Titans’  season opener, a non-conference home game Aug. 21 against Class 5A-affiliated Floyd Central, which won the IHSAA Class 5A Sectional 16 title a year ago. The Titans are ranked No. 2 in the 2026 Indiana Football Coaches Association Class 3A preseason poll. “This is a really-fun group to coach, and I thought that we had a great week one (of official practice),” said Hart of the Titans’ preparations. “They’re a group that has fun competing and getting after it, and they enjoy it. They’re a highly-motivated group that I’ve not had to ask them to get going even one time. They’ve really attacked this first week, which is great." “Even though we graduated a bunch of guys, we also have guys stepping up into new spots. I thought we did some good things on both sides of the ball,” said senior OT Ben Reinhart following the Maroon-Gold game. “Our defense came up with some interceptions, and we scored some touchdowns. We still have some things to work on, but I thought we played pretty hard.” “Overall, I think our defense played really well,” said senior DT/DE Khale Campbell after the intrasquad scrimmage. “We have some minor things to work on that we’ll learn from and fix. The offense competed and went as hard as they could today, which really helped the defense get better. Overall, I think it was a really-good Maroon-and-Gold game.” “We still have a lot that we need to fix, clean up and get better at,” Hart added, “but we don’t have to ask this group to play hard. They’ve got that piece, and we work on and fix the things that we need to. We’ve got to keep getting better and fix some of the mistakes we’re making, but I feel like we’re ahead of where we thought we would be at this point of the season, so that’s always a good thing. With our schedule (which begins with playing 2025 5A Sectional Champion Floyd Central in Week 1 and Missouri powerhouse St. Pius X in Week 2 in the United Fidelity Bank Bowl), our guys are going to have to be ready to go right away.” “All summer, we’ve been working hard, and I thought we had a pretty good week one,” said Reinhart in describing the Titans’ preparations for the season ahead. “We’ve really been getting after it and competing throughout the summer and through week one,” added Campbell. “Yes, we graduated quite a few guys, but guys are working hard to step up and fill those roles. We’ve just got to continue to fight and improve so that we can be ready for Week 1.” As for this year's seniors, “They’ve exceeded my expectations, and they’ve really set the tone for our football team,” noted Hart. “They just go and attack every day and give it everything they have. Our seniors have done a really-great job so far.” Senior QB Caden Rochleau (22-for-41; 261 passing yards; 4 passing TD, 4 INT; 158 yards rushing, 1 rushing TD as a junior), after filling in for Wabash College football signee Zach Foster (197-for-310; 2164 yards passing, 29 TD passes, 10 INT; 1061 yards rushing; 9 rushing TD as a senior) following Foster’s injury in the regional championship game, made his first-career varsity start in the 2025 South Semi-State championship game and is set to fully take the reins of the Titans’ offense. “I couldn’t be more proud of Caden,” said Hart. “He’s stepped up and kind of taken that role head-on. He’s got all the talent in the world, and he’s done a great job of taking care of the football throughout the whole summer. I thought that in our first offensive drive (of the Maroon-Gold Game), he was surgical in the passing game and in the RPO game. He made great decisions and was getting the ball to where it needed to go. He was running our offense very well and very clinically. His understanding of the position, and his decision-making, continues to grow and progress.” “Caden’s really been getting after it all summer,” noted Reinhart. “He’s continued to step up and grow. He’s really committed to putting the work in and doing the best he can for our team so that we can be as successful as possible.” “Caden was thrown into a tough position (following the injury to Zach Foster), but he’s really worked his tail off to earn the position,” noted Campbell. “I’ve definitely seen growth in him. He’s determined, and he wants to win and help lead the team. It’s definitely a good mindset to have.” At running back, the Titans look to veteran backs in senior Eli Foster (378 yards rushing as a junior) and junior Tucker Deputy (274 yards rushing; 5 rushing TD as a sophomore) to fill the production provided by Hanover College football signee Colin Scherer (835 rushing yards; 14 rushing TD; 11 catches, 90 receiving yards as a senior), though Deputy has also transitioned into more of a role in the Gibson Southern linebacker corps. Others to watch include sophomore Makade Malone. “I think we’ve got a really nice stable there,” said Hart. “Eli brings a lot of experience and runs hard, and Makade Malone brings a speed factor to the backfield, and then we have Tucker, who ran it some last year. He’s more on the defensive side of things now, but we have the ability to bring him over, as well. We have three really-good guys back there to run the football for us.” “I think our run game has been solid so far,” added Reinhart. “Eli’s been pretty good, and he gives us a ton of experience in that spot. Overall, I think our running-back room is looking pretty good, which gives us confidence as an offensive line.” “I’m really happy Eli is there in the backfield,” said Campbell. “He’s a great fit at that position, and we feel confident that the rest of the room will continue to step up and grow.” With graduation of key contributors such as WR Noah Kuester (57 catches, 640 yards receiving, 13 TD receptions), WR/H-Back Toby Pullum (38 catches, 333 yards receiving, 6 TD receptions), WR Jake Mazzier (23 catches, 208 yards receiving, 1 TD reception) and WR Lloyd Sellers (28 catches, 394 yards receiving, 4 TD receptions), the Titans’ leading returning receiver is senior Peyton Johnson (42 catches; 483 yards receiving; 5 TD receptions as a junior). “Peyton’s had a great summer,” noted Hart. “He’s a guy that kind of gives us an A.J Brown-ish kind of receiver. He can take the top off of the defense and go get it, but as a big, strong, guy, he can break tackles and also give us those tough yards on the outside after catching hitches and curls.” Others to watch for in the receiving corps include juniors Ayden Bodrie and Luke Mallory, as well as senior Elijah Ortiz, junior Isaac Dill and junior Austin Smith. “Ayden and Luke are both very athletic and do a good job of going up and catching the football,” said Hart. “We’re looking to see who emerges and how that rotation works itself out.” “I feel like our receiving corps is going to be explosive and exciting this year,” described Reinhart. “They’ve all got big-play ability, especially with Caden’s arm strength. Peyton is back, and he was a big piece of our offense last year. We have a lot of guys competing for spots, which will be good for our team.” “Overall, I think our receivers are ready,” added Campbell. “Peyton is back, which is a big help. All the guys competing for those spots are ready to go.” While the Titans graduated three-fifths of last year’s offensive-line starters in LT Spencer Staggs, LG Blake Ulm and C Bobby Robinson, Gibson Southern returns starters in junior RG RJ Smith and senior RT Owen O’Neal to a new-look quintet in the trenches. Senior Ben Reinhart, who split time between tight end (5 catches, 39 yards in 2025) and defensive end (12 total tackles; 1 tackle for loss; 1 pass break-up - ahead of the Semi-State) as a junior, made the transition to serving as a full-time offensive lineman and looms at left tackle. Hart noted that competition is ongoing between the trio of Nathan Emery, Eli Bodrie and Jadyn Kiefer to determine who will emerge with the additional starting positions on the offensive line. “We’re continuing to get better there every single day,” said Hart. “Our pass protection is probably ahead of our run game at the moment. Over the next couple of weeks, we have to keep focusing on getting better up front in the run game. We had a couple of nice plays today, but we need to be able to run the football more efficiently and effectively than where we are after week one (of official practice).” “We graduated three guys on the left side of the line,” noted Reinhart, “but we get RJ and Owen back, which is huge for us. I kind of knew that I would be making the switch to the offensive line ahead of time. We also have a bunch of new guys that are hungry and looking to step up and earn those spots.” “The people that have filled in have stepped up to (try and) earn those positions,” added Campbell. “Guys are continuing to compete and fight for their spots. With who we have on the O-Line now, I feel like those guys are ready to go.” Following graduation of a senior-laden defense that featured Lindsey Wilson football signee and four-time All-State DT Brody Klem (65 total tackles; 28 TFL; 7 sacks; 1 forced fumble - ahead of the Semi-State), MLB Colin Scherer (116 total tackles; 10 TFL; 4 PBU; 2 INT; 2 fumble recoveries - ahead of the Semi-State) and DB Lloyd Sellers (state-leading 10 interceptions in 2025), the Titans look to a returning senior starter on each level in DT Khale Campbell (50 total tackles; 17 TFL; 5 sacks - ahead of the Semi-State - as a junior), LB Ian Maikranz (66 total tackles; 3 TFL; 1 INT; 4 PBU - ahead of the Semi-State - as a junior) and S Cole Ridens (59 total tackles; 4 PBU - ahead of the Semi-State - as a junior) to lead the way for a new-look group on that side of the football. Others competing for defensive-line spots alongside Campbell include senior DT Gavin McEllhiney, junior DT Isaac Peach, sophomore DE Lincoln Plasse and sophomore DE Reed Luecke. “It’s been great competition,” noted Reinhart of the Titans’ offensive and defensive lines competing against one another. “Iron sharpens iron, as I like to say. We push each other to play hard and make positive strides every day. We have guys on the D-Line that are hungry and looking to make an impact.” “We have some decent size up front, but I think overall as a defense, we’re a lot more athletic, maybe, than what we usually are,” noted Hart. “That’s something that really stands out. Those guys are really able to run around and chase things down. As a whole, our defense flies around and makes plays. It’s a group that I’m really excited about. This is a group that, throughout the summer and through week one, has been able to run the ball particularly well on us. We still have some work to do, but our front-seven has done a really good job of playing the run so far.” “We have some younger guys on the line,” noted Campbell, “but they have the right mindset of doing what it takes to win. We’ve been attacking every day in practice, and we’re ready to just go, go, go.” As for the Titans’ linebacker corps, “Ian played outside last year, but we’ve moved him to ‘Mike’ this year, and he’s done a great job in there,” noted Hart. “He’s been the quarterback of the defense for us and gets us where we need to be. “Tucker Deputy has moved over from running back, and then junior Gabe Foster and junior Max Brink are competing, as well,” Hart added. “As a whole, our linebackers have played really well. I really like where we are there in terms of athleticism. That group is possibly as athletic a group that we’ve had there in a while from a strength and speed standpoint. They do a great job of flying around.” “Ian has stepped up, and that group as a whole is really going and competing on every play,” noted Campbell. “They’re doing their jobs well and getting their jobs done.” “Those guys are battling every day and continuing to get better,” said Reinhart of the linebacker corps. The Titans’ secondary team is battling through various injuries ahead of the 2026 campaign, said Hart. “It’s been a mix-and-match type of thing there so far,” Hart said. “Cole Ridens is back as a starter at safety, and Elijah (Ortiz) played a lot of safety last year, as well. Having two guys at safety with that level of experience is huge.” At cornerback, “Isaac Dill started a couple of games last year,” added Hart. “(Junior) Eli Stone and (junior) Kaigan Nossett have also done a fantastic job so far. We’ve got a little depth there. “As a whole, and as a team, there are some guys that have stepped up over the summer and through this first week that we weren’t sure were going to get there,” Hart said. “We have to keep building competitive depth across the board, especially with the way that we want to play. A lot of guys have continued to step up and work hard as we go into the season.” “I’m really proud of those guys. The guys in the secondary are really competing and fighting to earn their spots,” noted Campbell. “I feel like we’re pretty strong in the secondary.” Rochleau returns as the team’s punter, but the competition for the remainder of the Titans’ special teams’ positions is ongoing following the graduation of senior PK Will Redden (59-for-61 PATs, 3-for-5 FGs in 2025), a three-sport All-Gibson County athlete a year ago (football, soccer and golf), as well as Mazzier, a Western Kentucky University Baseball signee and the 2025-26 Princeton Clarion Gibson County Male Athlete of the Year, who played a key role in the return game in 2025. Hart noted that Jeter Simmons, a Princeton Clarion All-Gibson County and All-Pocket Athletic Conference performer on the soccer pitch, looms as the team’s kicker in filling that role in a similar fashion to what Redden did a season ago. “Jeter is new to us, and he had a good day today (Saturday at the Maroon-Gold Game), where he didn’t miss one, which I thought was great” noted Hart. “For a guy that’s never really kicked before (on the football field), he’s really been consistent throughout the opening week. He’s come out and has done a great job." “Jeter’s stepped up and earned that position,” noted Campbell. “He’ll be ready to go.” “Caden’s got a great leg as our punter,” shared Hart. “He’s an athletic guy, and it’s always good to have a guy that is as athletic as him as your punter. He did a great job last year, and he’s continued to do a great job so far there.” Lincoln Plasse, who has been “really consistent so far here, early in the process,” said Hart, looms as the team’s long snapper, while Elijah Ortiz looms as a candidate to return punts, while Isaac Dill and Makade Malone loom as potential candidates as kickoff returners. Special teams “is something that we spend a lot of time on and want to be good at, although it’s maybe the toughest thing to simulate and get a good live look at at this point of the year,” said Hart. “We won’t fully know what we have there until we get into that Week One game. Through the first week (of official practice), I really like where we are in the kicking game.” “It starts up front in the trenches on both sides of the ball,” said Reinhart in describing the keys to the Titans having success in 2026. “If we want to be successful, we have to dominate up front.” “We’ve just got to keep going, keep driving and putting in the work every day,” concluded Campbell. “We’ve got to keep building and getting better each day,” concluded Hart, “and we need to make sure, as we go along with the season, that we have guys continue to step up and play at a high level, week-in and week-out. We’re going to compete. This group will always compete really hard. We’re going to find out right away where we stand. Per a recently released Goldman Sachs report, “Global M&A volumes rose 48% YoY against an unusually supportive backdrop,” which was “driven primarily by the surge in deal size, with mega M&A volumes +125% YoY.” And the firm expects that strength to continue, saying that the M&A cycle has “substantial room to run, despite long-standing geopolitical and inflationary pressures.” Further, we’re witnessing a historical IPO market (which is great for the underwriters), as the recently completed second quarter saw nearly $116 billion in IPO proceeds (largely driven by the SpaceX IPO), which marks the second-highest quarterly total this century, behind only the first quarter of 2021 (at $133 billion). Should dealmaking continue apace, and should we see the much-anticipated IPOs of Anthropic or OpenAI emerge, it looks like the environment should remain supportive for investment banks. With that in mind, let’s take a look at two of Wall Street’s heaviest hitters when it comes to dealmaking: Goldman Sachs (GS) and Morgan Stanley (MS). MS has been the better performer over the last year, rising 49.5% compared to 43.5% for GS. But over the last five years, Goldman Sachs has handily outperformed the competition, with a 151.2% gain compared to Morgan Stanley’s 106.9% increase. That said, both stocks are trading just off their all-time highs, so if you were inclined to give the round to MS, I wouldn’t argue. While dealmaking fees are independent of an investment bank’s book of assets, P/B is still a reality check for banks. On that lens, GS looks less stretched than MS. MS offers a modestly higher dividend yield, but if your 2026 thesis includes “higher-for-longer rates plus decent equity returns,” that extra yield can be meaningful—especially if deal volumes don’t accelerate as quickly as hoped. MS is more popular among institutional investors, who hold meaningfully more of the “float” (publicly available shares) than they do in GS. But that can cut both ways, as it suggests deep sponsorship and broad index/fund participation (often supportive in drawdowns) but can also mean more “crowding” (less incremental buyer power and more selling “ammunition” if sentiment flips). Goldman Sachs is the 800-pound gorilla when it comes to investment banking and is routinely at the top of the heap when it comes to total volume. In the first half of 2026, Goldman advised on an astronomical $1.3 trillion in deals (per this scorecard from dealogic), which put them well ahead of Morgan Stanley’s $880 billion. That follows a 2025 in which Goldman was also at the front of the pack ($1.6 trillion in deals vs. Morgan Stanley’s $1.1 trillion), and a similarly weighted 2024 ($968 billion for Goldman; $744 billion for Morgan Stanley). These are both heavy hitters, but Goldman leaves the competition in the dust, and when advisory and underwriting activity rises, the bank that’s already winning the biggest mandates tends to capture a disproportionate share of the incremental fees. And that’s especially important this year, which has seen an increase in the number of large deals and a decrease in the number of smaller mergers. title: GS Power Partners Names Michael Smith CEO as Jason Kuflik Becomes Executive Chairman - citybiz
content: GS Power Partners has named Michael D. Smith president and chief executive officer, bringing in an energy industry veteran to lead the New York-based distributed solar company as it works to expand its project portfolio following a $250 million corporate financing. Smith assumes the role effective Aug. 10, succeeding co-founder Jason Kuflik, who is transitioning from CEO to executive chairman. Kuflik will remain involved in the business, focusing on key external relationships while continuing as a significant shareholder. The leadership transition comes as GS Power Partners moves into a new growth phase. The company recently completed a $250 million corporate loan facility with Deutsche Bank and has established a five-year value creation plan focused on executing its development pipeline and scaling operations. Smith brings more than 25 years of energy industry experience, including leadership roles in distributed energy, solar and energy storage. Most recently, he served as CEO of CPower Energy, a distributed energy resource monetization provider with more than 6 gigawatts of capacity across nearly 20,000 customer sites. The business works with distributed energy resources to participate in energy markets and grid programs. Before CPower, Smith was CEO of ForeFront Power, a developer of distributed solar and energy storage projects in the U.S. and Mexico. He previously held senior positions at Constellation and Exelon, including serving as senior vice president of distributed energy and leading Constellation Technology Ventures. That background gives Smith experience across several parts of the distributed energy market as GS Power Partners looks to convert its development pipeline into additional operating assets. GS Power Partners develops, finances, owns and operates commercial and industrial and community solar projects across the United States. Founded in 2015, the company has focused on North American distributed generation solar rather than utility-scale development. Its current portfolio includes more than 400 megawatts of operating projects across more than 125 projects and 40 funds, with most of its assets concentrated in the Northeast and Midwest. Kuflik helped build the company’s development platform, assemble its team, secure capital and establish its investment strategy. As executive chairman, he will continue supporting the company’s relationships while Smith takes responsibility for day-to-day leadership and execution of its growth plan. The succession also follows institutional backing for GS Power Partners from CVC DIF, a global investment firm with nearly €23 billion in assets under management. Combined with the Deutsche Bank loan facility, that capital structure provides the company with resources to pursue its existing pipeline and expand its distributed generation portfolio. Smith’s appointment puts an executive with experience scaling distributed energy businesses at the center of that effort, while retaining Kuflik in an active role as the company moves from its founder-led phase toward its next stage of development. © Copyright 2012 - 2026 | citybiz | Terms of Service | All Rights Reserved

title: Fans Choose Karol G’s Album ‘No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto’ as Best New Latin Music of the Week - Billboard

The album earned more than 60% of the vote in the latest Billboard New Music Latin poll. Karol G has topped Billboard’s new music Latin poll published on Aug. 7 with her sixth studio album, No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto. Billboard readers voted for the 14-track set as their favorite music release of the week after the New Music Latin poll and playlist was published; the album earned more than 62 percent of the vote. title: LS Electric, GS E&C Partner on DC Power Distribution for AI Data Centers - thelec.net
content: LS Electric and GS Engineering & Construction (GS E&C) have agreed to collaborate on direct current (DC) power distribution technology and power equipment supply for artificial intelligence (AI) data centers. LS Electric said on Aug. 10 that it signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with GS E&C to jointly respond to changes in the AI data center business environment. Under the agreement, the companies will develop next-generation DC power distribution technologies aimed at improving power efficiency in high-power, high-density AI data centers. As part of the partnership, LS Electric will supply key electrical equipment for AI data center projects being developed by GS E&C, including switchboards, gas-insulated switchgear (GIS) and extra-high-voltage transformers. LS Electric is currently developing DC power distribution products such as solid-state transformers (SSTs), solid-state circuit breakers (SSCBs) and energy storage systems (ESS). The company has also established a production facility at its Cheonan site in South Chungcheong Province that operates entirely on a DC power distribution system. An LS Electric official said demand for DC power distribution technologies is increasing as operators seek to improve the power efficiency of AI data centers.

title: GS E&C, LS Electric team up on AI data center power systems - The Korea Herald
