Business GS E&C, LS Electric team up on AI data center power systems Inside Korea’s chaebol leadership and tech industry Partnership covers equipment supply and next-generation solutions for global tech clients GS Engineering & Construction said Monday it is teaming up with LS Electric to strengthen the power infrastructure for its artificial intelligence data center projects. Under a memorandum of understanding, the two companies will establish a supply framework to ensure the timely delivery of key electrical equipment from LS Electric for AI data center projects under development or planned by GS E&C. They will also explore next-generation power solutions. AI data centers require greater power density and cooling capacity than conventional cloud data centers because they operate large clusters of high-performance computing equipment, including graphics processing units. Securing sufficient electricity and building reliable substation and distribution infrastructure are critical to their development and operation. GS E&C and LS Electric plan to hold technical exchanges on modular data centers and direct-current power distribution systems to meet the growing power demands of AI workloads. The companies will also work together to address the design and technical requirements of major customers, including global technology companies, and to supply power equipment for future AI data center projects. The partnership is part of GS E&C’s effort to strengthen its position in the AI data center business, which is emerging as a new growth engine for the builder. “Power infrastructure is a key factor in determining the success of an AI data center project,” a GS E&C official said. “Through this partnership, we will continue to strengthen our competitiveness by cooperating not only on the supply of power equipment, but also on next-generation power solutions and the technical requirements of global customers.” Incheon overtakes Heathrow as world’s busiest international airport Incheon Airport overtook London Heathrow and Singapore Changi to become the world’s busiest international passenger hub in the first half of the year, reaching No. 1 just 25 years after opening. title: Mailbag: Vikings 2026 Night Practice Offers Unique Start to Preseason Opening Week vs. Giants - Minnesota Vikings
content:
Do you have a comment or question? Send it to the Mailbag. Every Monday we'll post several comments and/or questions. Click here to submit a comment or question to Mailbag. Remember to include your name and town in the email. If Twitter / X is your jam, you can send a question to me that way as well. The annual night practice of Vikings Training Camp was held Sunday, providing an enthusiastic introduction to Minnesota's first week of the preseason, which will culminate at noon (CT) Saturday when the Vikings visit the Giants for both teams' first preseason game of 2026. Players are off today and will return to action Tuesday, the first of three days of practices, before flying to the New York area Friday. That also means that an unofficial (you can bold that word, underline or highlight it, or do all three) depth chart is likely to be unveiled this week ahead of the preseason opener (if history holds true). Be on the lookout for that, and make sure to tune in for Saturday's game, which will air in the Twin Cities market on KMSP FOX 9. Because of the timing of the night practice and the perpetual camp to-do list, this Mailbag will be a little shorter than most. View photos of Vikings players during Training Camp Night Practice on August 9 at TCO Stadium. Training camp is on, and everyone's spirits and expectations are high across the league. Players, coaches and the NFL fanbases are all excited. This was how I felt last August. Then a number of injuries and re-injuries to the O-line had me asking my brother if a team has ever drafted all offensive linemen in a draft before. I know some fans want to blame all struggles on QB and injuries there, which was part of it, but a protected QB in an O'Connell offense will burn any defense in the league with Jets and Jordan Addison on the field. We saw Sam Darnold crumble under exotic pressures against the Lions and Rams (twice each), and we've seen the same for his multiple replacements. I honestly think the 2026 Vikings will go as far as their O-line takes them. Based on camp so far, is there a position or group we should be more worried about or keyed into? How has Blake Brandel looked at center? Chances of getting any other veteran depth at center or guard before the season starts? Cheers to Brian O'Neill and his new contract. I hope our trenchmen stay happy and healthy throughout the season. Skol! The lack of continuity at QB in the 2023 and 2025 seasons has been a big talker, especially when compared to the results the team put together in 2022 and 2024 when the starter was able to go the full season. But the B-topic that provides context and nuance that many on social media and/or TV do not have time for was just how rough a go the o-line had in 2025, which counteracted the Vikings best-laid plans for a second-year QB coming off missing his rookie season with a knee injury. There were just 83 snaps played together by the intended starting five of Christian Darrisaw, Donovan Jackson, Ryan Kelly, Will Fries and O'Neill, and there were 26 combinations across the five positions.
